chunks: ہم سے محمد بن ابراہیم بن اسحاق (رحمۃ اللہ علیہ) نے بیان کیا۔ کہا: ہم سے احمد بن محمد ہمدانی نے بیان کیا۔ کہا: ہمیں احمد بن صالح بن سعد تمیمی نے خبر دی۔ کہا: ہم سے موسیٰ بن داؤد نے بیان کیا۔ کہا: ہم سے ولید بن ہشام نے بیان کیا۔ کہا: ہم سے ہشام بن حسان نے بیان کیا، حسن بن ابی حسن بصری سے، عبد الرحمن بن غنم دوسی سے۔ کہا:

معاذ بن جبل رسول اللہ (صلی اللہ علیہ وآلہ) کی خدمت میں روتے ہوئے حاضر ہوئے۔ انہوں نے سلام کیا تو آپ نے جواب دیا۔ پھر فرمایا: اے معاذ تمہیں کیا رلاتا ہے؟ کہا: اے رسول اللہ، دروازے پر ایک نرم بدن، صاف رنگ، خوبصورت شکل والا نوجوان ہے جو اپنی جوانی پر ایسے رو رہا ہے جیسے بیٹا کھونے والی ماں اپنے بچے پر روتی ہے، اور آپ سے ملنا چاہتا ہے۔ تو نبی (صلی اللہ علیہ وآلہ) نے فرمایا: اے معاذ اس نوجوان کو میرے پاس لاؤ۔ تو اسے آپ کے پاس لے آئے، اس نے سلام کیا تو جواب دیا۔ پھر فرمایا: اے نوجوان تمہیں کیا رلاتا ہے؟

کہا: میں کیسے نہ روؤں جبکہ میں نے ایسے گناہ کیے ہیں کہ اگر اللہ عزوجل مجھے ان میں سے بعض پر بھی پکڑے تو جہنم کی آگ میں ڈال دے، اور مجھے نہیں لگتا کہ وہ مجھے ان سے نہ پکڑے، اور مجھے کبھی نہ بخشے۔ رسول اللہ (صلی اللہ علیہ وآلہ) نے فرمایا: کیا تم نے اللہ کے ساتھ شرک کیا ہے؟ کہا: میں اللہ کی پناہ مانگتا ہوں کہ اپنے رب کے ساتھ شرک کروں۔ فرمایا: کیا تم نے کسی ایسی جان کو قتل کیا جسے اللہ نے حرام کیا ہے؟ کہا: نہیں۔ نبی (صلی اللہ علیہ وآلہ) نے فرمایا: اللہ تمہارے گناہ بخش دے اگرچہ وہ بلند پہاڑوں جیسے ہوں۔ نوجوان نے کہا: وہ پہاڑوں سے بھی عظیم تر ہیں۔ نبی نے فرمایا: اللہ تمہارے گناہ بخش دے اگرچہ سات زمینوں اور ان کے سمندروں، ریتوں، درختوں اور مخلوقات جیسے ہوں۔ کہا: وہ ان سے بھی عظیم تر ہیں۔ نبی نے فرمایا: اللہ تمہارے گناہ بخش دے اگرچہ سات آسمانوں اور ستاروں اور عرش اور کرسی جیسے ہوں۔ کہا: وہ ان سب سے بھی عظیم تر ہیں۔

So the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) looked at him angrily, then said: Woe to you, O youth! Are your sins greater, or your Lord? So the youth fell on his face saying: Glory be to my Lord! Nothing is greater than my Lord. My Lord is greater, O Prophet of Allah, than every great thing. So the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: Can anyone other than the Great Lord forgive the great sin?! The youth said: No, by Allah, O Messenger of Allah. Then the youth went silent. So the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said to him: Woe to you, O youth! Will you not tell me of one of your sins?

He said: Of course, I will tell you. I was a grave robber for seven years. I would exhume the dead and take their shrouds. A young woman from the daughters of the Ansar died. When she was carried to her grave, buried, and her family left, and night fell, I came to her grave and exhumed her. Then I took her out and removed her shrouds, leaving her bare at the edge of her grave. I went to leave, but Satan came to me and began making her attractive to me, saying: Do you not see her stomach and her whiteness? Do you not see her hips? He did not stop saying this until I returned to her, and I could not control myself until I had relations with her and left her in her place. Then I heard a voice from behind me saying: O youth, woe to you from the Judge of the Day of Judgment, the day He raises me and you just as you left me naked among the dead, exhumed me from my grave, stripped my shrouds, and left me in ritual impurity before my Judgment. Woe to your youth from the Fire. I do not think I shall ever smell the scent of Paradise. What do you see for me, O Messenger of Allah?

So the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: Get away from me, O wicked one! I fear that I will get burned by your fire. How near you are to the Fire! How near you are to the Fire! Then he (peace be upon him and his family) did not stop speaking and pointing at him until the youth left his presence. He went to Medina, gathered provisions from it, then went to one of its mountains to worship therein. He wore a hair cloak,

and bound his hands together to his neck, and called out: O Lord, this is Your servant Bahlul, bound before You. O Lord, You are the One who knows me, and my errors that You know of. O my Master, O Lord, I have become one of the regretful, and I came to Your Prophet repentant, but he sent me away and increased my fear. So I ask You by Your name, Your majesty, and the greatness of Your power, do not diminish my hope, my Master, and do not invalidate my supplication, and do not deprive me of Your mercy. He did not stop saying this for forty days and nights. The wild animals and beasts would weep for him. When forty days and nights had passed, he raised his hands to the sky and said: O Allah, what will You do regarding my need? If You have accepted my supplication and forgiven my sin, then send revelation to Your Prophet. And if You have not accepted my supplication and not forgiven my sin, and You want my punishment, then hasten a fire to burn me or a punishment in this world to destroy me, and deliver me from the disgrace of the Day of Resurrection.

So Allah, Blessed and Exalted, revealed to His Prophet (peace be upon him and his family): 'And those who, when they commit an indecency' — meaning fornication — 'or wrong themselves' — meaning by committing a sin greater than fornication, grave robbing, and taking shrouds — 'remember Allah and seek forgiveness for their sins' — meaning they feared Allah and hastened to repent — 'and who can forgive sins except Allah?' He said, Mighty and Majestic: My servant came to you repentant, O Muhammad, and you sent him away. Where would he go, to whom would he turn, and whom would he ask to forgive his sin besides Me? Then He said, Mighty and Majestic: 'and those who do not persist in what they have done while they know' — meaning they no longer commit fornication, grave robbing, or taking shrouds — 'their reward is forgiveness from their Lord and gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they shall abide eternally, and excellent is the reward of the doers of good' (3:135-136).

When this verse was revealed to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), he went out reciting it and smiling. He said to his companions: Who will direct me to that repentant youth? Mu'adh said: O Messenger of Allah, we were told he is in such-and-such place. So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) went with his companions until they reached that mountain. They climbed it searching for the youth, and there they found the youth standing between two rocks, his hands bound to his neck, his face blackened, his eyelashes fallen from weeping, and he was saying:

My Master, You have perfected my form and made my appearance beautiful. So I wish I knew what You intend for me — will You burn me in the Fire, or will You settle me in Your proximity? O Allah, You have bestowed much goodness upon me and blessed me. So I wish I knew what my end will be — will You escort me to Paradise, or drive me to the Fire? O Allah, my sin is greater than the heavens and the earth, and Your vast Seat and Your great Throne. So I wish I knew — will You forgive my sin, or will You scandalize me with it on the Day of Resurrection? He did not stop saying things like this while weeping and pouring dust on his head. The wild animals surrounded him and the birds lined up above him, weeping at his weeping. So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) drew near, freed his hands from his neck, cleaned the dust from his head, and said: O Bahlul, rejoice, for you have been freed by Allah from the Fire.

Then he (peace be upon him and his family) said to his companions: This is how you redress your sins, just as Bahlul redressed them. Then he recited to him what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed about him and gave him glad tidings of Paradise.

ai.summary: یہ ایک ڈرامائی روایت ہے جس میں بہلول نامی نوجوان نبی اکرم (صلی اللہ علیہ وآلہ) کے پاس قبر کشائی اور لاش کی بے حرمتی کے سنگین گناہوں پر گہری پریشانی میں آتا ہے۔ نبی اکرم نے ابتدا میں اسے خوف سے دور بھیج دیا، بہلول نے پہاڑوں میں چالیس دن شدید توبہ کی۔ اللہ تعالیٰ نے سورہ آل عمران 135-136 نازل فرمائی۔
